summary: UFC Freedom 250 was held on the White House South Lawn on 14 June 2026, Trump's eightieth birthday. The FBI director said the bureau became aware of the threat on 10 June; arrests were made over that weekend in Ohio, Missouri, Nebraska and California; five people were in custody and investigators identified twenty three people as part of a potential network of plotters. The event went ahead without incident.
rationale: The dated pre-commitment is real and verifiable. On 10 June 2026 at KvS6uzzLK6c@4436 he said he had been told again to pray for the fourteenth, four days before the date, and the fourteenth is the day a disrupted plot was aimed at. The FBI became aware on the same 10 June, though not publicly. Held at partial rather than strong for three reasons. He named only a date and no event, place, method or threat: things about the 14th is the whole content. The fourteenth was already the most conspicuous date on the American calendar that month, being the president's eightieth birthday with a UFC event on the White House lawn that had been covered in advance including a US News preview on 12 June, so a prophetic voice praying over the fourteenth was not selecting an obscure day. And what he asks prayer for is unspecified, so any outcome on that date would have been claimable.

summary: Five men were charged over the plot, named as being from Ohio, Missouri, Nebraska and California. Coordination took place in a TikTok group before moving to Signal, with one large chat of about nineteen people and smaller groups of four to five. Eight were eventually indicted.
rationale: Scored against the specific number he asserts. On 19 June he says all twenty three of them are now in custody. Twenty three is a real reported figure, but it is the size of the network investigators identified, not the number detained: five were in custody at that point and eight were eventually indicted. He states it after the reporting was public, so the number was available to be read rather than seen. The claim as worded is false on the record, and the pre-commitment row above should be read with this beside it.

summary: The alleged plan was to fly drones laden with explosives over buildings near the White House event, force a mass evacuation and drive the fleeing crowd toward a pre-staged sniper team, with a second wave planned to storm the White House gate.
rationale: The method matches closely: explosive drones detonated over a crowd at a public holiday event, which is what the standing claim describes. Held at partial because three parts do not match. The claim placed it in Europe with men buying drones online, and this was America with a domestic paramilitary cell. It was disrupted rather than carried out. And drone risk at large American public events had been publicly flagged by DHS in advance, so the threat category was not an unusual thing to name.

summary: The Department of Justice charged five men across four states in a plot to attack and kill government officials and others attending the UFC event at the White House, describing a four tier paramilitary structure that pooled money for tactical gear and mapped drone launch and sniper positions.
rationale: On the claim as originally worded, cells of people with ill intentions already inside the country, found and brought to justice, this is a match. It fails on the specifics he added later. He said the actors would be foreign infiltrators and an act of war rather than terrorism; the men charged are Americans across four states. He said there would be no internet chatter from an ISIS enthusiast to warn of it; the group organised on a public TikTok group before moving to Signal, and reporting says a warning from one suspect's mother helped foil it. The chatter is how they were found, which is the opposite of what he specified.
